title: AWS Examples
description: Small AWS examples from the lessons. Each example links back to its explanation and practice task.

examples.title: What AWS provides
examples.description: Amazon Web Services offers rented computing and storage. You choose services for a job and pay according to their rules and usage.
examples.code:
Need: share a static reading page
Possible parts: object storage and a content delivery service
Practice today: draw the plan only

examples.title: Regions and Availability Zones
examples.description: An AWS Region is a geographic area. It contains separate Availability Zones designed to reduce shared failure risks.
examples.code:
Region: eu-west-1
Availability Zone: eu-west-1a
Plan: keep related practice resources in a chosen Region

examples.title: Identity and access with IAM
examples.description: IAM controls who can do what in AWS. A policy grants actions on resources. Least privilege means granting only needed actions.
examples.code:
Reader needs: read one approved object
Reader does not need: change account settings or delete a bucket

examples.title: S3 objects and buckets
examples.description: Amazon S3 stores objects inside buckets. An object has a key, which is its name within a bucket. Slashes in keys can look like folders.
examples.code:
Bucket: fictional-club-assets
Object key: pages/index.html
Object data: the page file

examples.title: Object access and versioning
examples.description: S3 access settings decide who can read an object. Versioning can retain earlier versions, but it is separate from access control and backup planning.
examples.code:
Object: pages/index.html
Version A: old heading
Version B: corrected heading
Access: remains controlled separately

examples.title: EC2 virtual machines
examples.description: An EC2 instance is a virtual machine. You choose its size and operating-system image, then remain responsible for much of its software upkeep.
examples.code:
Planned instance: small Linux VM
Job: a separate learning experiment
Needed upkeep: updates, permissions and monitoring

examples.title: VPCs and subnets
examples.description: A Virtual Private Cloud is a network space you configure. A subnet is a range of network addresses inside that VPC and one Availability Zone.
examples.code:
VPC range: 10.0.0.0/16
Example subnet: 10.0.1.0/24
Location: one chosen Availability Zone

examples.title: Security groups filter traffic
examples.description: A security group controls allowed traffic for attached resources. It is stateful: replies to allowed traffic are handled as part of that connection.
examples.code:
Example web rule: allow TCP 443 from the intended clients
No rule: unrestricted administration from the whole internet

examples.title: CloudFront caches content
examples.description: CloudFront is a content delivery service. It can serve cached copies from edge locations nearer to visitors.
examples.code:
Visitor -> nearby edge cache
Cache miss -> approved origin
Response -> visitor

examples.title: CloudWatch observations
examples.description: CloudWatch provides metrics, logs and alarms for supported resources. A metric is a number over time; an alarm checks a condition.
examples.code:
Metric: request errors per minute
Alarm condition: errors exceed the chosen threshold
Response plan: inspect logs and recent changes

examples.title: Budgets are alerts
examples.description: A budget helps track spending and can notify you when a threshold is reached. An alert is not automatically a hard spending stop.
examples.code:
Monthly learning limit: a fictional 5 currency units
Alert threshold: 80 percent
Alert point: 4 units

examples.title: Plan a static site carefully
examples.description: A cloud design should name the needed services, access rules, costs and cleanup steps. Keep a static learning site as static files.
examples.code:
Files: HTML, CSS, JavaScript and images
Access: read-only delivery to visitors
Origin: approved static-file storage
Review: domain, HTTPS, cache rules, cost
